campbell.title: Campbell City Council — September 1, 2026
campbell.summary: The Campbell City Council considered a resolution authorizing an agreement with the Santa Clara Valley Transportation Authority to receive Low Carbon Transportation Operations Program funding for a transit reliability and performance improvement project. The agenda also referenced pothole damage claims processes.
keyTopics: Resolution to authorize execution of a Low Carbon Transportation Operations Program fund agreement with VTA for transit reliability and performance system improvements
Pothole damage claims process

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — September 16, 2026
saratoga.summary: The Saratoga City Council took up several routine approvals, including meeting minutes, vendor payments, and final map approvals for lot splits on Carniel Avenue and Saratoga-Los Gatos Road. The Council also considered two appeals of Planning Commission decisions on residential development projects, and discussed law enforcement service options ahead of upcoming public town hall meetings.
keyTopics: Appeal of a Design Review and setback variance for a house and ADU at 14650 6th Street
Appeal of a Tentative Map and Design Review approval for a three-lot subdivision at 14486 Oak Place
Law enforcement service options for the City, in preparation for town hall meetings on September 19 and 30
Final map approvals for two-lot subdivisions on Carniel Avenue and Saratoga-Los Gatos Road
Resolution amending the City's Conflict of Interest Code

los-altos.title: Los Altos City Council — September 8, 2026
los-altos.summary: The Los Altos City Council considered several routine administrative items, including updated employee pay schedules, a contract increase for an electrical maintenance vendor, and a resolution renaming Lee Street to Tubman Street. The Council also took up a citizen initiative on zoning impacts, discussed the future of the Environmental Commission, and prepared direction for upcoming regional CalCities meetings.
keyTopics: Resolution renaming Lee Street to Tubman Street
Citizen initiative on potential impacts to zoning
Contract amendment adding $250,000 to Bear Electrical Solutions' maintenance agreement
Restructuring of the Joint Volunteer Awards Committee into a Los Altos-only committee
Discussion on the Environmental Commission and possible formation of a Council subcommittee

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — September 15, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The Los Gatos Town Council reviewed routine business at this meeting, including approval of minutes from earlier September sessions and a monthly financial report for July 2026. The Council also considered several contract items, including amendments to service agreements and a heating/ventilation/air conditioning (HVAC) contract, along with new professional services agreements.
keyTopics: Approval of minutes from the September 1, 2026 Town Council and Closed Session meetings
July 2026 Monthly Financial and Investment Report
Second amendment to an existing town agreement
First amendment to a Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HVAC) services agreement
New professional services agreements for the town

san-jose.body: Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole
san-jose.title: San José Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole — September 16, 2026
san-jose.summary: The Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole reviewed the upcoming September 22 and September 29, 2026 City Council agendas, including whether to add items or set specific meeting times. The committee also considered several special event approvals for use of city funds and donations, plus a proposed item on safety standards for self-checkout systems at grocery and drug stores.
keyTopics: Review and updates to the September 22 and September 29, 2026 Council agendas
Free use of the Janet Gray Hayes Rotunda for a November 19, 2026 Realtors Association event sponsored by Council District 9
Retroactive approval of a Council District 4-sponsored Santos Family Car Show as a city special event
Retroactive approval of various Council District 5-sponsored special events
Proposed self-checkout safety standards for grocery and drug retail stores

mountain-view.title: Mountain View Youth Advisory Committee — September 14, 2026
mountain-view.summary: The Mountain View Youth Advisory Committee met to open the floor for public comments, take part in a team-building exercise, and discuss its proposed work plan for the 2026-27 fiscal year. Committee members also shared updates and comments before wrapping up the meeting.
keyTopics: Public comment period (Oral Communications)
Team Builder activity for committee members
Fiscal Year 2026-27 Youth Advisory Committee Work Plan
Committee member and staff comments/reports

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — September 15, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: The Sunnyvale City Council considered several routine and policy items, including a large equipment purchase for the sewer department, a road resurfacing contract, and salary schedule changes for certain management employee groups. The Council also considered renaming a water treatment facility, revising several council policies (including changing the meeting start time to 6 p.m.), and held a TEFRA hearing on tax-exempt bond financing for a 123-unit affordable housing project.
keyTopics: Purchase of a $793,417.50 combination jet/vacuum sewer cleaning vehicle for Environmental Services
Award of a $951,353.25 contract for the Homestead Road slurry seal paving project
Rejection of all bids received for the Plaza Del Sol Phase II project
Renaming the Donald M. Somers Water Pollution Control Plant to the Sunnyvale Donald M. Somers Clean Water Facility
TEFRA hearing on tax-exempt bond financing for a 123-unit affordable rental housing project at 245 W. Weddell Drive

cupertino.title: Cupertino City Council — September 15, 2026
cupertino.summary: The Cupertino City Council met to discuss real estate negotiations for a property on Finch Avenue with the Cupertino Union School District, along with potential litigation in closed session. The public meeting covered several routine items including an AI use policy for the Council, a response to a county grand jury report on pothole damage claims, and appointments to a subcommittee for selecting the city's next legislative lobbyist.
keyTopics: Closed session on anticipated litigation and real property negotiations for 10480 Finch Avenue with Cupertino Union School District
Recognition of Cupertino High School students for their FBLA National Leadership Conference achievements
Adoption of a new Artificial Intelligence (AI) City Council Policy
Approval of the city's response to the Santa Clara County Civil Grand Jury report on pothole damage claims processes
Appointment of Mayor Moore and Councilmember Wang to a subcommittee evaluating city lobbyist proposals for 2027-2028

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara City Council — August 25, 2026
santa-clara.summary: The Santa Clara City Council held a special meeting that combined Civil Service Commission interviews with a joint session with the Stadium Authority Board. The agenda covered board and commission appointments, several recognitions, a janitorial services contract amendment, a historic preservation agreement, and routine reports and approvals.
keyTopics: Interviews and appointment of two applicants to the Civil Service Commission (one partial term through 2028, one full term through 2030)

Recognition of outgoing commissioners from the Library Trustees, Civil Service, Cultural, Historical and Landmarks, Parks and Recreation, and Senior Advisory commissions, plus recognition of 2026 Mission Meets the Moment campaign sponsors
Authorization for the City Manager to negotiate and execute amendments to the citywide janitorial services agreement with Impec Group, Inc.
A Mills Act historical preservation agreement for the property at 1261 Jackson Street
Review of board, commission, and committee annual workplans for FY 2026-2027, and designation of a voting delegate and alternates for the League of California Cities

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — September 15, 2026
milpitas.summary: The Milpitas City Council considered several financial and infrastructure items, including federal community development grant funding, red light camera safety data, and the condition of the Milpitas Community Center. The council also took up bond refunding and other business tied to the former redevelopment agency's successor agency.
keyTopics: Draft Program Year 2025 Community Development Block Grant Consolidated Plan
Presentation on the Red Light Camera Traffic Safety Program
Presentation on the condition of the Milpitas Community Center
Resolution of the Successor Agency to the Redevelopment Agency
Sale and issuance of refunding bonds for the Successor Agency

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto Planning & Transportation Commission — September 9, 2026
palo-alto.summary: The Palo Alto Planning & Transportation Commission considered an ordinance amending the Municipal Code to address City Council direction on the separate sale of accessory dwelling units (ADUs). The Commission also received a Director's Report covering meeting scheduling and assignments, and reviewed draft minutes from its August 12, 2026 meeting.
keyTopics: Proposed ordinance amending Titles 18 and 21 to regulate separate sale of accessory dwelling units (ADUs)
Director's Report on meeting schedule and commissioner assignments
Approval of draft summary minutes from the August 12, 2026 meeting
